content.thinking:
I'm thinking through a whimsical capybara design, exaggerating real proportions into a blocky head, round barrel body, and tiny legs with a cheerful warm brown/tan palette, maybe adding a small companion bird for charm.

I'm now sketching the pose details — webbed toes, markings, whiskers, a flower behind the ear — then roughing out skeleton coordinates for the body, spine chain, and head placement to build the rig.

Adding a tiny tail stub joint for rigging, then laying out a short neck chain from chest to head base, with the head aimed slightly downward and jaw, ears, eyes, and four leg chains to follow.

For the body, I'm reconsidering how to position hips and sweep the body shape from rump to chest using the spine chain as the loft path, with rounded caps at each end to get the capybara's rump and chest contours right.

For the head, I'm planning to loft it separately along a head-to-neck chain so it joins seamlessly, giving it that large, boxy shape with a blunt snout — sweeping an elliptical cross-section from the skull down to the nose with radii tapering appropriately.

Profile-wise, the top runs nearly straight from the forehead to a tall, bulging muzzle, with eyes set high, small ears at the rear top, and nostrils up front. I'm setting up loft stations from skull to nose with elliptical widths/heights, using rounded circle sections rather than sharp boxes for a whimsical look, rigged to a head joint, and now I'm starting on the jaw.

The jaw needs its own lower loft from the jaw joint forward, with a lighter tan tone and a thin dark sweep marking the mouth line, plus tiny visible incisors and a dark rounded nose pad with paired nostrils. For whimsical proportions, I want a round barrel body, stubby legs, a big head, and exaggerated puffy cheeks.

For the face, I'm giving it big shiny black eyes with white highlights and half-lidded brow caps in the coat color, creating that relaxed, content capybara look. Then I'm adding a tiny perched songbird on the head's crown, built from a round body sphere, head, cone beak, wedge tail, extruded wings, eyes, and little feet, all needing their own joint hierarchy for the body, wings, tail, and head.

For the bird's colors I'm picking a blue-teal back, cream belly, orange cheek patch, and tiny crest tuft, sized up a bit for whimsy at roughly 0.14-0.15m tall against the capybara's 0.25m-wide head. Now I'm settling on the capybara's warm color palette — reddish-brown coat, darker back, lighter tan belly, dark muzzle, and brown-pink ears — leaning into a brighter, whimsical tone overall.

Fur will use small tapered strand cards scattered across the body, around 700 of them at 4 tris each for about 2800 tris total, plus a mottled grain paint technique for hair streaks and a slightly darker spine stripe. For the feet, I'm giving front paws 4 digits and hind paws 3, with light webbing and small claws.

Still figuring out toe joints...

Actually, I'll simplify and just manually place toe joints per foot with explicit positions and aim directions, using a "digit" role, counting 14 total joints across front and hind feet. Now I'm working out leg geometry—shoulder and foot target positions, leg lengths—to set up the front legs.

Positioning the rump slightly higher than the shoulders for the natural capybara slope, then setting up leg chains with joint names for shoulder-elbow-wrist, tapering limb thickness toward the paw, and placing flattened paw shapes with toes so the feet rest flush on the floor.

Now I'm planning head details: skull loft, cheek puffs, muzzle block, dark nose pad with nostrils, a philtrum line splitting the upper lip, whiskers as thin tapered rods on both sides plus chin whiskers, eyes with lids and highlights, brows, small rounded ears with pink inner color, the distinctive morrillo scent-gland bump on the nose for male capybaras, and incisors -- plus a whimsical flower tucked behind one ear.

Working out the flower geometry: a small ring of petals extruded outward from the ear, oriented so the outline runs along the radial and tangent directions with thickness following the flower's normal.

For fur, I'm thinking of using tapered strand cards scattered over the body surface, colored by tinting a grey-to-white gradient with the coat paint color, keeping counts modest for a low-poly fuzzy edge look.

For facial details I'll add decal-based features: pale freckle spots, pink translucent blush ellipses on the cheeks, sphere-based eyes, and a curved stroke smile decal to give the capybara a whimsical, content expression.

The jaw needs to be a separate sweeping part from the joint forward, so I'm figuring out the joint position and direction in model coordinates to keep it aligned with the head.

Working out explicit skull loft stations with widths and heights to shape the upper head, making sure the lower bound meets up cleanly with where the jaw attaches below.

Let me rework the body proportions bigger, with center y 0.37 and height 0.46, giving a top around 0.60 with modest belly clearance, matching real capybara shoulder heights of roughly 50-62 cm scaled whimsically. I'm placing the head center around y 0.48 with crown near 0.58, keeping it carried low and forward so the head top sits roughly level with the back, and nose center near 0.43.

I'm now mapping out head cross-sections at several z-depths, adjusting their centers, heights, and widths so the skull tapers forward, then separating out the lower jaw as its own sweep along the bottom-front rather than folding it into the skull shape.

Still shaping the jaw sweep... Now I'm considering fluffed cheek ellipsoids near the jaw area and thinking about how high-set capybara eyes should sit on the skull.

For the eyes, I'm using surface-hit placement around the skull at an azimuth and elevation to position them forward and slightly upward, then sticking in small dark spheres (bigger than realistic scale for whimsy) with tiny white highlight dots and a subtle upper lid cap.

Still working out eyelid geometry...

Now I'm positioning small rounded ears behind the eyes, oriented sideways with a slight outward tilt, shaping them as semi-ovals with smoothed edges and adding a thinner pink inner-ear layer slightly in front.

I'm placing the ears at the top sides of the skull, checking the geometry doesn't overlap with the flower ornament or bird sitting on top. I'm also adding the morrillo—the dark hairless gland capybaras have above their nose—as a flattened dark brown sphere, plus a darker nose pad at the front of the snout.

For the muzzle's end cap, I need to account for how the loft rounds off at the tip based on its radii, so I'm estimating the nose tip lands around z .88, keeping the head length proportional to a whimsical scaled-up capybara.

Now I'm roughing out the body stations connecting neck to rump, trying to keep total body length around 1.2-1.3 units by compressing the z-range between nose and rump rather than letting it stretch past 1.4.

I'll structure the spine as a 4-point chain producing three joints (spine1, spine2, spine3), with the hips serving as the root joint that the spine chain parents from. Then I move on to planning the neck chain, starting from the end of the spine toward a point higher and more forward.

For the neck, I decide on a 3-point path yielding two joints (neck1, neck2), parented to the last spine joint. I then define the head joint sitting at the top of the neck with an aim direction forward, and begin sketching the body loft path as a series of stations with varying widths and heights moving upward from the lower torso.

I want the spine chain and loft path to roughly align in position, so I adjust the spine joint coordinates to track near the loft station centers from hips through neck to head, making sure the bone hierarchy follows the body's visual shape reasonably well.

Now I'm thinking about the paint and leg setup: body coat paint follows the sweeps, and legs are built as limb-chain-sweep combinations attaching inside the torso near the shoulders and hips. I'm positioning front paws and hind feet, planning three-segment hind legs (thigh, shin, foot) with a plantigrade-ish hock to keep the capybara's stance believable.

Adding haunch and paw details...

Then I'll give toes small dark nail caps at their tips for the hoof-like look, add a tiny hairless tail nub joint, and move on to placing hair cards across the body, head, cheeks, and legs plus eyebrow whiskers.

For the hair cards I need separate scatter passes: a dense body scatter, a lighter leg scatter, and a head scatter filtered to the skull, keeping the lean angle so cards read well from the side. For extra whimsy I'm considering small touches like a passion-flower tucked behind the ear, but deciding to keep things simple and skip extras like a butterfly or extra birds beyond the one already planned.

I want the bird singing with an open beak, so I need to model it with separate upper and lower beak pieces, plus a body, head, wings, tail, and tiny legs with toes gripping the capybara's head. I'm also weighing whether to add a few grass-blade cards near the feet for storytelling detail, but need to watch the overall complexity budget.

Adding dark blue tail with crest spikes, orange feet, extruded teardrop wings with feather stripes, and fan-shaped tail wedges, then positioning the bird perched atop the capybara's head with its body tilted and head turned slightly for charm.

With part counts climbing toward 200 total (fur cards, whiskers, toes, bird details all adding up), I'm now defining the coat paint using a countershaded mottle texture layered with grain for the body surfaces.

For the face, I'm thinking a darker forehead and muzzle gradient over a lighter cheek tone to mimic real capybara coloring, plus small blush decals, while the legs darken toward the feet using a gradient fade. I'm also sketching out some SVG textures for strand, smile, and blush details.

Now I'm defining the fur card texture as a tapered SVG shape that gets tinted by the paint system, then moving into the joint/chain API for building the skeleton—setting up named joints with parent, aim, and role properties, and writing a loop to construct the left and right leg geometry using limb point arrays.

I'm checking that joint naming matches front versus hind limbs (shoulder/elbow/wrist vs hip/knee/ankle) and confirming the limb function's expected signature, then moving on to sweeping the leg chains with a radius function to generate the rounded limb geometry.

Now I'm thinking through toe digit joints parented to the wrist tip, and for the eye hit-testing I need to check whether `surface.around().at()` returns a nullable `Hit` so I can handle the null case properly. I should also grep for the `ik.ts` signature and option typings before wiring this together, and I don't think the toon kit is needed here.

input.command: ls; ls samples scratch 2>/dev/null | head -30; cat package.json | head -30
